answer: The orchard multiplier is published, charged in quill, and bridge lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2399 identities would post 1960 proofs and burn roughly 43 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
